IM-SAVED-01 · BUILD CONTRACT · BOARDS 107–124 · NATIVE DESIGN, NOT RUNTIME PROOF
Save the question. Refresh the evidence. Never freeze the answer.
Saved Research is a durable investigation workspace—not a bookmark to an old conclusion. It preserves the user’s question and research context, requalifies the latest evidence on open, and makes changes, exclusions and uncertainty visible before any new interpretation.
121 · Desktop · 1440
122 · Tablet · 768
123 · Mobile · 390
107–120 · State + write-effect specimens
WHAT IS SAVED
Question + research context
Stable record ID, question, canonical market/tool/measure references, period, currency and analytical filters. Focus, scroll and temporary view state stay session-local.
WHAT IS REFRESHED
Evidence + qualification
Current evidence generation, source/observation/release clocks, rights, coverage, revisions and qualified/excluded/removed changes.
WHAT IS NEVER IMPLIED
A frozen answer or hidden action
No saved conclusion, confidence score, live signal, alert, monitor, task, trade or investment recommendation is created by save, open, refresh or return.
Reopen flow · one question, qualified evidence
Read path until the user explicitly changes the saved record
01 · LOAD RECORD
Question + context
Stable saved ID
→
02 · FETCH EVIDENCE
Qualified generation
Rights + clocks
→
03 · QUALIFY
Supported / excluded
Never zero-fill nulls
→
04 · DIFF
Added / revised / removed
Saved baseline vs current
→
05 · CONTINUE
Current research read
Answer may stay partial
01 · CANONICAL OWNERS + IDENTITY
Reuse the existing owners. Do not create a second research store.
Reuse Terminal user-state ownership, not an assumed ready-made R10 API. Existing thesis saved views use workspace_settings but only retain thesis filters. R10 question/context persistence needs an explicit typed extension; domain evidence remains with its current owners. See source audit below.
PROPOSED R10 REFERENCE · NOT THE CURRENT THESIS FILTER PAYLOAD
schema_version · saved_research_id · owner_principal · question · market_refs · tool_id · selected_measure_refs · period · currency · analytical_filters · baseline_evidence_ref? · created_at · updated_at · version
Never store a rendered conclusion, a synthetic confidence number, or copied provider payload as the saved object.
02 · EVIDENCE GENERATION + CHANGE RECEIPT
Explain exactly what changed—and why it now qualifies or does not.
First release: compare the owner-backed evidence reference retained at save with the current qualified generation. Show “Compared with saved evidence”. Opening or refreshing never advances the baseline. Missing baseline means comparison unavailable—not zero changes. Keep every field’s observation, release and retrieval clocks.
ADDED
REVISED
EXCLUDED
REMOVED
A successful fetch that fails schema, rights or quality checks is not a successful evidence refresh.
03 · RESPONSIVE NAVIGATION + CONTINUITY
The layout changes. The research context does not.
Desktop 121 keeps inventory, selected research and evidence rail visible together. Tablet 122 compresses inventory into a narrow rail while preserving full selected-detail semantics. Mobile 123 prioritizes changed questions, then opens the existing reopened-detail route on Board114. The same saved record, query, measure selection and return target survive every transformation.
1440 · DESKTOP
Three-pane workspace
List · selected detail · clocks/actions
768 · TABLET
Rail + focused detail
List stays available without shrinking evidence
390 · MOBILE
Changed-first inventory
Open Board114 for the complete detail
Back/reload/auth return preserve saved record ID, inventory filter, selected record, measure IDs, locale, scroll and focus restoration target.
04 · STATE MODEL + HONESTY BOUNDARIES
Inventory, evidence and write effects are three separate state machines.
INVENTORY
loading · inventory · true empty · filtered empty · access required · unavailable — Boards107–113.
EVIDENCE
supported · not applicable · missing · stale · denied · failed · unknown, with field-level reasons — Board111.
WRITE EFFECT
review/confirm · outcome checking · success/undo · retry-safe failure · remove/undo — Boards115–120.
True empty follows a successful authenticated inventory read. Filtered empty preserves the underlying inventory. Access denial and network failure never masquerade as empty.
05 · EFFECT + RETRY BOUNDARIES
A read refresh and a saved-record write are not the same operation.
READ / REFRESH
Resolve current owner-backed evidence; reuse unchanged generations. Retry only failed source reads and ignore obsolete responses. No saved-record version or baseline change.
SAVE / EDIT
Review exact question/context/measure changes before one idempotent write. Use stable operation identity, outcome check, success receipt and undo window.
UNCERTAIN
Timeout after write dispatch is not failure proof. Check the original outcome before retry; never create a second record or silently advance the visible version.
Opening a question, reviewing changed evidence, using search, changing filters or returning to overview must never auto-save or create alerts, monitors, tasks or trades.
06 · ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE + PRODUCTION BOUNDARY
Native composition is reviewed. Real behavior still needs exact-path proof.
Responsive: 1440 / 768 / 390, then 320 and 200% text without deleting evidence or actions.
Interaction: keyboard, touch, focus order, screen-reader names, reduced motion and scroll restoration.
Data: added/revised/excluded/removed evidence, stale generations, rights denial, missing clocks and schema failure.
Auth + persistence: inventory load, true/filtered empty, sign-in return, version conflict, retry-safe failure, undo and no duplicate records.
Required real-path receipts: authenticated inventory owner, exact saved-record version, current evidence-generation ID, source clocks/rights/coverage, observed write outcome, back/reload restoration and zero hidden alert/monitor/trade effects.
These Paper boards do not prove backend migration, authenticated persistence, provider entitlement, functioning routes, runtime accessibility, browser behavior or investment accuracy.
Implementation rule · preserve one product brain.
Reuse domain truth and Terminal user-state ownership. Keep research intent durable, view mechanics session-local, and conclusions recomputed. The source audit below distinguishes real saved-view capability from the R10 extension still required. No new evidence store or parallel history plane.
NEXT IMPLEMENTATION SLICE
First bind the exact R10 reference schema to the existing user-state authority. Preserve RMS saved-view behavior. Then prove save → readback → reopen through Board114; no direct field stuffing into the thesis filter API.
124.7 · SOURCE VERIFIED · R10 INTEGRATION NOT YET PROVEN
Reuse the owner. Extend the contract—not the assumptions.
Source: mastermind-terminal · protected master c35b9a1d50ca4960c361645f0300fa9f95158a4e. These are repository observations, not a deployed-version or live-database receipt.
EXISTS IN SOURCE
Personal saved-view owner
terminal/app/api/thesis-saved-views/route.ts · terminal/lib/savedViews.ts
Authenticated personal records use workspace_settings and the rms_saved_view namespace. The route lists views and supports create, rename and delete. Its existing payload is a thesis-filter preset—not the International question, selected measures or evidence baseline.
Reuse responsibility, not a mismatched payload.
Preserve the existing RMS route and records. Qualify a typed R10 extension under the same user-state authority. No second authentication or saved-state service.
EXTENSION REQUIRED
A lossless research reference
terminal/lib/rmsViews.ts · normalizeViewFilter in savedViews.ts
The current filter whitelist retains lifecycle, staleDays, windowClosed and subjectGroupKey. It does not retain the R10 question, country, period, currency or selected measures. A successful existing create response is therefore not proof of a valid R10 save.
Version, validate, read back.
Use a discriminated R10 reference schema. Reject unsupported fields rather than silently dropping them. Read back every semantic field. Keep focus, scroll, temporary tabs and display mechanics in session navigation state.
PROOF STILL REQUIRED
Safe writes and recovery
createSavedView · renameSavedView · deleteSavedView
An optional client UUID is not a completed idempotency contract. Existing pre-read checks are not version-conditional writes; the saved-view cap check is not transactional. Full question edits, outcome lookup and undo are not exposed by this route.
Keep one original operation.
Bind request identity to user, record, operation and payload. Require version-conditional mutation, atomic limits and verified result receipts. After a timeout, resolve the original outcome before retry; undo is its own guarded write.
Do not reinvent recovery.
Existing reference: ThesisWorkspace.tsx and applyThesisVersion in lib/theses.ts use an owner-scoped request ID and expected version, then validate the thesis RPC receipt. Reuse the protocol pattern—not the thesis payload or lifecycle. This source read does not prove an R10 write.
First acceptance: one record survives the round trip.
Confirm → authenticated save → exact readback → reopen in Board114. Assert semantic fields and owner identity, then qualification and baseline diff, then browser return/accessibility. Preserve existing RMS behavior. No live integration is accepted by these design notes.
124.8 · ANALYTICAL READINESS · INDEPENDENT OF SELECTED-DATA COVERAGE
Qualified data can still leave the question unanswered.
Name the comparison before interpreting it.
For policy divergence: require both economy IDs, mapped comparable policy instruments, the selected definition, and aligned observations at two dates. Keep expected paths, nominal rates and real rates distinct. A domestic 10Y–2Y curve is not a cross-country policy-rate spread.
The Japan fixture remains 2 of 3 selected measures qualified. Its comparison economy is not selected, so answer readiness remains INCOMPLETE. Do not invent a denominator or infer low risk from a missing input.
Define “widening” rather than guessing the sign.
Signed gap: g(t) = rate A(t) − rate B(t)
Absolute widening: |g(end)| − |g(start)|
Use one unit throughout. For rates entered as percentages, multiply the percentage-point difference by 100 to display basis points. An increasing signed gap can be convergence when it starts negative. Show the metric definition and source cutoffs beside the result.
Example: a signed gap moving from −3.00 to −2.50 percentage points rises by 50 bp but NARROWS by 50 bp. Until comparison prerequisites qualify, show missing inputs and the next research action—not a directional conclusion.
Architecture alignment: Macro e4018a2b · agentos/decisions/DEC-RESEARCH-CONTEXT-IS-PORTABLE-REFERENCE-NOT-MEMORY.md. Persist bounded canonical references, not copied source bodies, rendered answers or raw UI state. Source rights and evidence qualification remain with their existing owners.
)
